terminal.description: A shell in the top folder. Run the setup once to build the shop's folder, then go into shop and work there with git.

tasks.title: Commit the new finds by themselves
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs` in the top folder, then work inside `shop`. Femi left three changes in the working folder: two new books in `finds.html`, a phone number in `visit.html` and a new page, `events.html`.

Make a commit that holds the new books in `finds.html` and nothing else.

The check finds the commit where both new books first appear in `finds.html` and expects no other file in it.
nextSteps: Run `git status` and find the three changes: two modified files and one untracked file.
Run `git status` again: `finds.html` is the only file under changes to be committed.
Commit it with a short message.
hints: A commit takes everything in the staging area, so what you stage decides what goes in.
`git add` with one file name stages only that file. `git add .` would stage all three changes.
Run `git add finds.html`, then `git commit -m "Add two finds for March"`.

tasks.title: Fix the phone number, then commit it by itself
tasks.description:
Femi typed the shop's phone number into `visit.html` with two digits swapped. Wilma's number is `01632 960 418`. Fix it in the editor and save, then make a commit that holds `visit.html` and nothing else.

The check finds the commit where `visit.html` first has Wilma's number and expects no other file in it.
nextSteps: Open `shop/visit.html` in the editor, correct the phone line and save.
Stage `visit.html` after the fix, not before.
Run `git status` to see that only `visit.html` is staged.
hints: The staging area holds a file as it was when you added it. Fix first, then stage.
If you staged visit.html before fixing it, git status lists it twice: once staged and once modified. Add it again to stage the fixed version.
Save the fixed file, then run `git add visit.html` and `git commit -m "Add the shop's phone number"`.

tasks.title: Stage the reading group page without committing it
tasks.description:
Wilma wants to read `events.html` before it goes into the history. Put it in the staging area, ready for the next commit, and do not commit it.

The check expects `events.html` in the staging area, in no commit, and still in the working folder.
nextSteps: Run `git status`: `events.html` is listed as untracked.
Run `git status` again and stop there: it is under changes to be committed.
hints: Staging and committing are two separate steps. This task is only the first one.
The same command that staged the other files stages this one.
Run `git add events.html`, and no `git commit` after it.
